Subject: Summit session — exec brief + demo ask

Hi team,

Thanks again for agreeing to present at the Acme Innovation Summit on June 6. A couple of asks from our side to make sure the execs and the product team are aligned:

- Can you provide a 1-page executive pocket brief we can hand out to the sponsor execs? Focus: value to Acme (latency/cost improvements, security posture).
- We need a tightly timed 3-minute live demo script and a 1-slide visual that maps to the demo steps.

Timing: would love the draft by EOD May 21 so we can circulate internally. Attaching the event brief and our buyer priorities for reference.

Attachments: Acme_RFP_QA.pdf (reference)

Let me know if you want a quick call — Jordan and I can jump on a 20-min check.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: Summit session — exec brief + demo ask

Emma — thanks, got this and the attached priorities. Quick plan below.

Draft plan (high level):
1) Pocket brief — single page, top section: one-line value prop + three bullets with quantifiable benefits (latency, cost per 1k tokens, compliance controls). Bottom: customer quote & one-paragraph Acme-specific play.
2) Demo script — 3 steps, each ~45s plus 15s transition: (a) 20s context, (b) 90s live request turnaround + latency highlight, (c) 50s fallback/failure demo + autoscaling mention.
3) Slide — single visual with annotated callouts tied to the script timestamps.

I'm attaching a first cut of the pocket brief (pocket-brief-draft-v1.docx) and a slide stub link. Marissa — can you add the customer story and tighten language? Karthik — can you review the demo timing and the run order with the ops notes?

If it helps, we can do a 30-min dry run on May 25 (morning PT) to validate transitions.

Attachments: pocket-brief-draft-v1.docx
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDeFGhIJkLmN

Thanks,
Irene Choi

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 9:15 AM Emma Torres <emma@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for agreeing to present at the Acme Innovation Summit on June 6.

Thanks — added a short customer story that maps to Acme's privacy-first ask (see paragraph 2). Suggestions:
- Lead with a one-line benefit targeted at infra execs: "Reduce inference cost per 1k tokens while holding latency under 50ms for core workflows."
- Customer quote (realistic, but anonymized): \"We saw inference cost drop 38% in production while improving p99 response time\" — attribute to "large retailer" unless Acme is ok with a named reference.
- Call out compliance: "VPC deployment + KMS/HSM support" as a bullet under controls.

Slide guidance: keep three annotated callouts with timestamps — don't put more than two code snippets. Visual: timeline bar with Step 1/2/3.

I made inline edits in the draft (tracked in pocket-brief-draft-v1.docx). Karthik — see the demo section where I suggested forcing a cold-cache path at the 2nd demo marker to highlight cache warmup improvements.

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Summit session — exec brief + demo ask

Irene/Marissa — thanks for the draft. Quick ops notes for the 3-min demo:

- Run order suggestion: 1) one-line context by Irene (15s), 2) live query against hosted API showing p50/p95 in the UI (75s), 3) fallback to Dedicated variant to show graceful degradation + autoscale event (60s), 4) closing KPI snapshot (30s).
- Trigger for fallback: simulate capacity routing by switching model endpoint (we'll pre-provision dedicated pool for the run). That gives us a real failover trace to show latency delta.
- Risk: network hiccup might lengthen the run. Plan B: pre-record the fallback clip and play if live run exceeds 3:30.

Attached updated demo script with cues and timing (demo-script-v2.md). Also added a short ops checklist for the dry run (May 25).

Attachments: demo-script-v2.md

Karthik Iyer
Director, Field Engineering, Redwood Inference
